en.title: Powder alert for Alpe d'Huez? 18–62 cm of fresh snow next week (23–29 November)
en.description: Alpe d'Huez snow forecast for 23–29 November 2026: 40 cm at the top (18–62 cm), 10 cm at the base, snowiest day Wednesday 25 November, with neighbours compared.
en.lede: Wednesday 25 November is the day to circle for Alpe d'Huez. It carries the biggest single share of next week's snow, and over the whole week of 23–29 November the top around 3200 m collects 40 cm (18–62 cm) while the base gets 10 cm.

p: At the top (around 3200 m) the week totals 40 cm, 18–62 cm across our range. Mid-mountain around 2200 m gets 35 cm (15–55 cm), and the base around 1200 m 10 cm (4–16 cm).

Most of the total arrives on Tuesday 24 (4 cm, up to 7), Wednesday 25 (11 cm, up to 12), Thursday 26 (11 cm, up to 17) and Sunday 29 (10 cm, up to 20), counted at the top as the middle of our forecast and the high case.

sections.h: Where the good snow will be
p: Wednesday 25 November is the snowiest day up top: 11 cm in the middle of our forecast and up to 12 cm in the high case. The morning after a snowy day is usually the one to ski, once lifts and patrols have caught up.

Go high: depth is safest on Pic Blanc and the Sarenne glacier, and the best skiing should be on the Pic Blanc and Sarenne side, before the sun works on the big south-facing bowl. Treat Vaujany, Oz and Auris on the lower edges of the domain as the weak point.

sections.h: Snow or rain at the bottom?
p: The base around 1200 m gets 10 cm against 40 cm at the top. That gap says the snow line sits above the village for much of the week: rain or wet snow down low, real snow only higher up.
The resort is known for its sunny aspect, which is lovely in March and harsh on fresh snow in November.
Same week, same measure (top of each resort): Les 2 Alpes (13 km away) 47 cm; La Grave (18 km away) 49 cm; Serre Chevalier (42 km away) 47 cm. Alpe d'Huez itself: 40 cm.
So La Grave is the better bet for fresh snow next week, if you are free to choose.

Next week does not start from scratch. From Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November our forecast gives the top 78 cm (52–103 cm) and the base 1 cm, the bigger fall of the fortnight. By the time the next round arrives, the upper mountain should already carry a real cover.

sections.h: The range, not just the number
p: The range is wide: 18 cm in the low case, 62 cm in the high one. That is normal a week ahead. The timing is more reliable than the total.
Book flexibly if you can: the picture for Alpe d'Huez will be much sharper by the weekend.

advice: Off the groomed runs, new snow means new avalanche risk: the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif is the reference.
Check the resort's own opening date and lift status: snow on the mountain does not mean lifts are running.
Pack for wet weather in the village: the 10 cm at the base hides a lot of rain.
